_comment: Tennessee statewide parcel boundaries, one pull per target area.
Tennessee publishes statewide parcel data for 86 counties through the
Comptroller's Division of Property Assessments, served on the TNMap portal.
One layer therefore covers every county below, which beats wiring up seven
separate county GIS servers with seven different schemas.
SET THE URL FIRST. The exact REST endpoint was not verifiable when this was
written, so it is a placeholder on purpose rather than a guess. Find it with:
gf find "tennessee property boundaries"
gf find "tennessee parcels" --kind arcgis
then paste the FeatureServer or MapServer layer URL, the one ending in a layer
number, into the url field of each source below. Then:
gf discover tn-parcels-davidson
Starting points to check: tnmap.tn.gov/arcgis/rest/services and the state open
data portal at tn-tnmap.opendata.arcgis.com.
WHY BOUNDING BOXES INSTEAD OF A COUNTY FIELD: a where clause needs the county
column name, which differs between layers and was not verifiable either. A
bounding box needs no schema knowledge at all, is applied server side so the
pull stays small, and is slightly over inclusive by design. The market filters
in config/markets.json do the precise work afterwards, so the extra parcels
cost a little bandwidth and nothing else.
Every box below is approximate. Widen any of them if a pull looks short.

sources.name: tn-parcels-davidson
sources.label: TN statewide parcels, Davidson County box
notes: Davidson also has its own county layer in davidson-tn.json, which may carry
richer fields. Try both with gf discover and keep whichever maps better.

sources.name: tn-parcels-williamson
sources.label: TN statewide parcels, Williamson County box, covers Fairview

sources.name: tn-parcels-cheatham
sources.label: TN statewide parcels, Cheatham County box, covers Pegram and Kingston Springs

sources.name: tn-parcels-spring-hill
sources.label: TN statewide parcels, Spring Hill box, Maury County side
notes: Spring Hill straddles the Williamson and Maury line. The Williamson side
comes in with tn-parcels-williamson, this covers the Maury side.
The county default here is Maury, so a parcel that is actually in Williamson
will be labelled Maury unless the layer publishes its own county column,
which the field mapper will prefer. Check that with gf discover.

sources.name: tn-parcels-old-hickory
sources.label: TN statewide parcels, Old Hickory Lake corridor
notes: The lake corridor crosses Davidson, Sumner, Wilson, Trousdale and Smith,
so no single county default is set here. The layer's own county column
should fill it in. Confirm with gf discover before relying on it.
This box is the whole lake corridor, which is a lot of inland parcels too.
After pulling, run 'gf geo --waterbody old-hickory-lake' and then filter
with --market old-hickory-waterfront to get down to the shoreline.
